rounds.text: Maximus International Ltd is fundamentally under-appreciated because its long-term growth trajectory significantly outpaces its current valuation, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow analysis suggesting an intrinsic value of Rs 24 per share compared to the current market price of Rs 17 [E39]. The company has demonstrated robust operational efficiency, consistently delivering a return on capital employed of 11.89% against a sector benchmark of 6.7% [E10]. This performance is supported by a strong multi-year sales uptrend, with compounded sales growth reaching 29% over the last five years and 30% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E16]. Furthermore, the company maintains a comfortable short-term liquidity position with a current ratio of 2.05x [E34]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow of Rs -8 Cr [E31], a lack of dividend payouts [E4, E46], and a recent deceleration in profit growth [E19, E55]. Despite these headwinds, the stock remains fundamentally attractive as historical profit growth of 24% over five years has significantly outpaced the 11% share price growth, indicating that the market has yet to fully price in the company's underlying expansion [E17, E20, E42].

The bull’s reliance on a DCF-derived intrinsic value of Rs 24 [E39] ignores the reality that the company is currently burning cash, with operating cash flow at Rs -8 Cr and free cash flow at Rs -4 Cr as of March 2026 [E31, E32]. While the bull highlights strong sales growth [E14, E16], this has failed to translate into bottom-line stability, as evidenced by a -17% contraction in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19]. Conceded: the company maintains a current ratio of 2.05x [E34]. However, this liquidity is overshadowed by the fact that borrowings have increased to Rs 52 Cr from Rs 39 Cr in just one year [E35], while the company simultaneously fails to provide any dividend yield to shareholders [E4, E46]. Furthermore, the bull’s claim that the market has not priced in expansion is contradicted by the fact that the stock is trading at 90% of its 52-week high [E5] and carries a P/E of 27.87x, which is significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 18.13x [E6]. Finally, the company’s operational quality is questionable given the high debtor days of 241 [E47] and the fact that promoters have been reducing their stake by 4.73 percentage points since December 2023 [E37].
